svg.text: Module 2 · Compute — What is a hypervisor and what is it for?
Based on “What is a Hypervisor?” (IBM Technology)
· VMs are added until the host is saturated
software that virtualizes the host: splits the CPU, “slices” the RAM, shares the network
Three paths to attach storage to a VM
Without a hypervisor: 1 box = 1 user. With a hypervisor: 1 box = N isolated VMs → multitenancy.
The hypervisor is the “magic layer”: virtualization → multitenancy → cheap compute.
AWS EC2 uses the Nitro hypervisor (KVM-based), type 1.
hypervisor as an app on the host OS
What it is for (in this course)
Multitenancy: many customers on the same host without
host ≈ $5,000 / month vs VM ≈ $50 / month (or free)
Every EC2 instance / Azure VM you launch in the labs is
an isolated VM on a type 1 hypervisor:
Lab 1 EC2 · HAProxy · BIND · Keycloak · VPC · Docker
slices of the host's CPU / RAM you get.
Isolation + resource sharing = key technology for the cloud.
